entry.title: The Not-So-Fine Print: How the FCA Makes Consumer Contracts Fair
entry.summary: The not-so-fine print: making consumer contracts fair FCA · Nov 6, 2026 · Guidance · CryptoTopic evidence: 「A crypto firm agreed to stop charging excessive storage fees which, in some cases, could exceed £40,000 a year.」 The UK Financial Conduct Authority explains how it checks whether terms in financial consumer contracts are fair and transparent under the Consumer Rights Act 2015. It gives examples including a crypto firm that stopped excessive storage fees, an adviser that dropped a complaint-handling charge, and a travel insurer that clarified unclear delay terms. It sets out what firms should do, such as using plain language and reviewing contracts regularly.

The rule expands prior authorization to additional Botulinum Toxin Injection services and allows hospital accrediting organizations to assess certain EMTALA administrative requirements during surveys. entry.title: Consultation conclusions on tightening limits on misleading names used by unregulated entities
entry.summary: SFC concludes consultation on further restricting use of misleading names by unregulated entities to protect investors SFC · Nov 6, 2026 · Guidance · CryptoTopic evidence: 「a similar provision under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO)」 The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) of Hong Kong published the conclusions of its consultation on restricting unregulated entities from adopting names that may falsely suggest regulated status. Respondents broadly supported expanding the restricted titles list under the Securities and Futures Ordinance and adding a similar provision to the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance. The SFC agreed to a faster list-update mechanism and plans to introduce an amendment bill to the Legislative Council.

An attached National Police Agency letter also outlines basic security measures for individuals and organizations.

entry.title: CFTC Issues Interpretation of Impartial Access Requirements
entry.summary: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation CFTC · Nov 5, 2026 · GuidanceThe Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued an interpretation of the impartial access requirement for designated contract markets. It states that geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with the Commodity Exchange Act and that requirement. Designated contract markets must stop domestic geographic restrictions that violate the requirement within 30 days or explain to the Division of Market Oversight why compliance is not feasible.

entry.title: CFTC Staff Letter on Trust Companies for Daily Settlements
entry.summary: CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements CFTC · Nov 5, 2026 · GuidanceOn November 5, 2026, the CFTC's Division of Clearing and Risk issued a no-action letter on whether derivatives clearing organizations may use trust companies for daily settlements with clearing members. According to the letter, such use is permitted if the clearing organization treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements.

entry.title: Treasury and IRS announce Opportunity Zone designations for more than 6,500 communities nationwide

A total of 6,576 eligible census tracts were nominated and designated, effective January 1, 2027, for ten years. The Working Families Tax Cuts permanently renewed the Opportunity Zone tax incentive, added enhanced incentives for rural investment, and established a process for redesignation every ten years.

entry.title: FCA acts to protect consumers facing repayment demands on disguised remuneration scheme loans
entry.summary: FCA acts to protect consumers facing demands for disguised remuneration scheme loan repayments FCA · Nov 5, 2026 · EnforcementAfter FCA intervention, Ethica Resolve Limited, an FCA-authorised debt collection firm, agreed to restrictions. It had demanded repayment of disguised remuneration loans, or purported loans, on behalf of West 28th Street Limited, which bought them from a third party. Under the agreed requirements, Ethica will tell affected consumers they have no enforceable payment obligation for now, will make no further payment demands in the proposed court claim, and will not seek default judgments.

entry.title: ADGM publishes guidance on crypto mining as the region's first such guidance
entry.summary: ADGM Becomes the Region's First International Financial Centre to Publish Dedicated Crypto Mining Guidance 28 Oct 2026 ADGM / FSRA · Oct 28, 2026 · Guidance · CryptoTopic evidence: 「the Guidance treats crypto mining as a licensable commercial activity overseen by the RA and not a regulated financial service」 The Registration Authority of Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) has published its Guidance on Crypto Mining Activities in and from ADGM. Issued under section 23 of the Commercial Licensing Regulations 2025, it treats crypto mining as a licensable commercial activity overseen by the RA rather than a regulated financial service. The guidance applies a technology-neutral approach covering Proof-of-Work, Proof-of-Stake and future consensus mechanisms.

entry.title: UK FCA to set up quantum computing group to explore tackling financial crime
entry.summary: FCA to explore quantum computing to tackle financial crime FCA · Nov 5, 2026The UK Financial Conduct Authority will bring together financial firms, quantum technology providers and national research laboratories in a Quantum Experimentation Group. The group will initially explore how quantum machine learning could help detect money laundering and fraud, using an FCA synthetic dataset. It is due to launch in the first quarter of 2027, and organisations can register interest by 31 December 2026.

entry.title: Looking back to move forward: why reviewing rules matters
entry.summary: Looking back to move forward: why reviewing our rules matters FCA · Nov 5, 2026 · GuidanceThe FCA explains why it regularly reviews its rules as markets, consumer behaviour and technology change. It describes its Rule Review Framework, which uses evidence assessments, post-implementation reviews and impact evaluations. Examples include mortgage rule changes, Senior Managers and Certification Regime reforms, wholesale transaction-reporting changes and IPO research rules.

entry.title: Speech by SFC Chairman Kelvin Wong at PWMA Wealth Management Summit 2026: When information is abundant, judgment becomes scarce
entry.summary: New speech by Kelvin Wong: Keynote speech at PWMA Wealth Management Industry Summit 2026 SFC · Nov 5, 2026 · SpeechIn a keynote speech at the Private Wealth Management Association's 2026 summit, SFC Chairman Dr Kelvin Wong argues that AI is making information abundant, so judgment, accountability and trust become the scarce assets. He says future wealth managers will act as conductors of technology while focusing human effort on complex decisions and relationships. The speech also highlights Hong Kong's opportunities as a cross-border wealth hub.

entry.title: IRS reminds tax preparers to renew 2027 PTINs before Dec. 31, 2026 expiration

entry.title: SFC Chairman Kelvin Wong's welcome remarks at a 2026 investment summit forum, 'Beyond the Familiar: A Fresh Look at Asia'
entry.summary: New speech by Kelvin Wong: Welcome remarks at “Conversations with Global Investors” forum of 2026 Global Financial Leaders’ Investment Summit SFC · Nov 4, 2026 · SpeechHong Kong SFC Chairman Dr Kelvin Wong gave welcome remarks at the "Conversations with Global Investors" forum of the 2026 Global Financial Leaders' Investment Summit. entry.title: CFTC Wins Court Order Requiring Texas Man and Firm to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud Case
entry.summary: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud CFTC · Nov 3, 2026 · EnforcementThe Commodity Futures Trading Commission announced a default judgment from the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas against Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for a commodities fraud scheme. The court found they solicited and misappropriated over $3 million from participants through false trading claims, Ponzi-like payments, and personal use of funds. The defendants were ordered to pay a $9,767,625 civil penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution, and were permanently enjoined and banned from trading and registration.

entry.title: CFTC Chairman Selig statement on perpetual futures for individual stocks

entry.title: CFTC Interim Final Rule Excludes Casino-Style Gambling From the Swap Definition
entry.summary: CFTC Issues Interim Final Rule Excluding Certain Activity from the Definition of Swap CFTC · Oct 10, 2026 · RuleThe Commodity Futures Trading Commission issued an interim final rule stating that casino-style gambling products, including sportsbook and casino game wagers, are excluded from the definition of "swap." The rule codifies the agency's longstanding position. It takes effect upon publication in the Federal Register, and written comments are due within 30 days via Regulations.gov.
